From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: MAP kickoff: initial MAP draft + timeline options (Aurora Health)

Hi Alex / Samantha / Jordan —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call yesterday. Per our conversation, I’m sharing an initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and a couple of timeline options so we can align on milestones, owners, and any blockers. Please find the MAP attached (Aurora_MAP_Draft_v1.xlsx).

Quick recap from the call:
- Goals: pilot Redwood inference for patient-facing triage flows (latency target < 200ms tail).
- Key success criteria: accuracy on our eval set, integration with Aurora’s HIPAA-safe VPC, and monitoring + cost targets.
- Top risks/dependencies: procurement timeline, legal review for DPA/K data residency, SOC2 evidence request.

Initial MAP (high level) — please confirm/edit owners:
1) Discovery & POC scope (Owner: Aurora product / Redwood AE) — Deliverable: acceptance criteria & test prompts — Target: week 1
2) Security & Compliance review (Owner: Aurora security / Redwood security) — Deliverable: SOC2 + architecture diagram + data handling doc — Target: weeks 1–3
3) Pilot deployment & integration (Owner: Aurora infra / Redwood eng) — Deliverable: working endpoint in Aurora VPC, basic observability — Target: weeks 3–6
4) Contract & procurement (Owner: Aurora procurement / Redwood legal) — Deliverable: signed SOW + purchase order — Target: weeks 4–8
5) Pilot validation & production rollout (Owner: Aurora product / Redwood CS) — Deliverable: go/no-go checklist + runbook — Target: week 8–10

Timeline options:
- Aggressive: 6 weeks to pilot (fast-track procurement/PO within 3 weeks) — target signature: 2026-04-30
- Conservative: 10 weeks to pilot (standard procurement cycle) — target signature: 2026-05-14

Ask: can you confirm the following by EOD Thursday?
- Stakeholders to include on the MAP (procurement, legal, security, infra, product) and their contact emails
- Which timeline you prefer (aggressive vs conservative) or a suggested target close date
- Any blockers we should add to the dependencies list (e.g., on-prem approvals, data residency constraints)

Next proposed step: 30–45 min MAP kickoff with all named stakeholders to finalize owners and target dates. I’m available Tue/Wed next week. If that works for you, I’ll send a calendar invite and attach updated MAP v2 after we agree on stakeholders.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this kicked off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: Aurora_MAP_Draft_v1.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, MAP milestones & owners)

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: initial MAP draft + timeline options (Aurora Health)

Thanks Marissa — useful summary and appreciate the draft. A few notes from our side: 
1) Please add our procurement lead Jordan Carter (jordan.carter@aurorahealth.com) to the MAP (cc’d on this thread). I’ve also looped in Samantha (product) but we need Legal on the next update — I’ll provide the contact once I have confirmation.
2) Data residency: our legal/security teams will expect explicit language around logs and retention. That’s a dependency — can Redwood provide a short data handling addendum or SOC2 snapshot?
3) Timeline: procurement has a 2–3 week internal review cadence right now, so the aggressive target of 2026-04-30 is likely unrealistic. Can we target 2026-05-14 for contract signature? If Redwood can support a quicker procurement Q&A turnaround (SLA on evidence requests), that would help.

We’re generally excited to move forward — happy to join a kickoff with stakeholders. For next steps, please add Jordan + Legal when you share MAP v2 and propose 2–3 times for the kickoff meeting.
